questions.stem:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Phenol on treatment with $CHCl _3$ /aq. KOH under refluxing condition, followed by acidification produces $p$-hydroxy benzaldehyde as the major product and $o$-hydroxy benzaldehyde as the minor product.
Statement II : The mixture of $p$-hydroxybenzaldehyde and $o$ hydroxybenzaldehyde can be easily separated through steam distillation.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below

options.label: A
options.content: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

options.label: B
options.content: Both Statement I and Statement II are true

options.label: C
options.content: Both Statement I and Statement II are false

options.label: D
options.content: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.solution:
Phenol with $CHCl_3$ / aq. KOH is the Reimer–Tiemann reaction.
The base generates dichlorocarbene: $CHCl_3 + OH^- \rightarrow :CCl_2 + Cl^- + H_2O$.
The phenoxide ion attacks $:CCl_2$ mainly at the ortho position; the $K^+$ ion coordinates both the phenoxide oxygen and the carbene, which directs it to the ortho carbon.
Hydrolysis of the $-CHCl_2$ group and acidification gives $o$-hydroxybenzaldehyde (salicylaldehyde) as the major product and $p$-hydroxybenzaldehyde as the minor product.
Statement I reverses the major and minor products, so it is false.
In $o$-hydroxybenzaldehyde, $-OH$ and $-CHO$ form an intramolecular H-bond (chelate ring), which makes the ortho isomer steam volatile.
In $p$-hydroxybenzaldehyde, molecules form intermolecular H-bonds and associate strongly, so the para isomer is not steam volatile.
Steam distillation therefore separates the two isomers easily, so Statement II is true.
Answer: (D) Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.stem:
3, 3-Dimethyl-2-butanol cannot be prepared by :
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

image.alt: Figure for this Alcohols Phenols And Ethers question

questions.solution:
Target: $(CH_3)_3C-CH(OH)-CH_3$ (3,3-dimethyl-2-butanol).
A: $(CH_3)_3C-CHO + CH_3MgBr \xrightarrow{H_3O^+} (CH_3)_3C-CH(OH)CH_3$, so A gives the target.
B: The alkene is $CH_3CH_2C(CH_3)_2CH=CH_2$ ($C_7$). Hydration gives only a $C_7$ alcohol, so B cannot give the target.
C: Ozonolysis of $(CH_3)_3C-C(CH_3)=CH-C(CH_3)_3$ gives $(CH_3)_3C-CO-CH_3 + (CH_3)_3C-CHO$. $NaBH_4$ reduces the ketone to the target, so C gives the target.
D: $LiAlH_4$ reduces $(CH_3)_3C-CO-CH_3$ to $(CH_3)_3C-CH(OH)CH_3$, so D gives the target.
E: $Hg^{2+}/H^+$ hydration of $(CH_3)_3C-C\equiv CH$ gives the ketone $(CH_3)_3C-CO-CH_3$, not the alcohol. So E cannot give the target.
Only B and E fail.
Answer: (A) B and E only

questions.stem: A hydroxy compound $( X )$ with molar mass $122 g mol ^{-1}$ is acetylated with acetic anhydride, using a large excess of the reagent ensuring complete acetylation of all hydroxyl groups. The product obtained has a molar mass of $290 g mol ^{-1}$. The number of hydroxyl groups present in compound $( X )$ is:
questions.solution:
Concept: acetylation turns each $-OH$ into $-OCOCH_3$. In effect, the H of each OH is replaced by an acetyl group, $CH_3CO$.
Mass gained per $-OH$ group: $M(CH_3CO) - M(H) = 43 - 1 = 42\ g\ mol^{-1}$
Total mass gained: $290 - 122 = 168\ g\ mol^{-1}$
Number of $-OH$ groups: $n = \dfrac{168}{42} = 4$
Check: a tetrol with $M = 122$ fits erythritol, $C_4H_{10}O_4$ ($4\times12 + 10 + 64 = 122$). Its tetraacetate has $M = 122 + 4\times42 = 290$, which matches.
Answer: (B) 4

questions.stem:
Consider the following reaction sequence
$\underset{[76.6\%\ \mathrm{C},\ 6.38\%\ \mathrm{H},\ \text{vapour density}\ 47]}{\text{Compound (x)}} \xrightarrow[(ii)\,\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{O}^{+}]{(i)\,\mathrm{CO}_2,\ \mathrm{NaOH},\ 120^{\circ}\mathrm{C},\ \text{high pressure}} \text{Compound (y)}$
develops characteristic colour with neutral $\mathrm{FeCl}_3$ solution.
Identify the INCORRECT statement from the following for the above sequence.

options.label: A
options.content: Compound y will dissolve in $\mathrm{NaHCO}_3$ and evolve a gas.

options.label: B
options.content: Compound x is more acidic than compound y .

options.label: C
options.content: Both compounds $x$ and $y$ will dissolve in NaOH .

options.label: D
options.content: Both compounds x and y will burn with sooty flame.

questions.solution:
Molar mass of x: $M = 2 \times \text{VD} = 2 \times 47 = 94\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$
Number of C atoms: $\dfrac{0.766 \times 94}{12} \approx 6$
Number of H atoms: $\dfrac{0.0638 \times 94}{1} \approx 6$
O makes up the rest: $94 - 72 - 6 = 16\ \mathrm{g}$, i.e. 1 O atom. So x is $\mathrm{C_6H_6O}$, which is phenol.
With $\mathrm{CO_2}$ and NaOH at $120^\circ\mathrm{C}$ under pressure, then $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$, phenol undergoes the Kolbe–Schmitt reaction. So y is salicylic acid (o-hydroxybenzoic acid). Its phenolic –OH gives a violet colour with neutral $\mathrm{FeCl_3}$.
(A) Salicylic acid ($pK_a \approx 3$) is a stronger acid than $\mathrm{H_2CO_3}$. It dissolves in $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$ and releases $\mathrm{CO_2}$ gas, so A is correct.
(B) Phenol ($pK_a \approx 10$) is a much weaker acid than salicylic acid ($pK_a \approx 3$). So B is incorrect.
(C) Both phenol and salicylic acid are acidic enough to dissolve in NaOH, so C is correct.
(D) Both are aromatic compounds with a high C:H ratio, so both burn with a sooty flame. D is correct.
Answer: (B)

questions.solution:
Key idea: controlled oxidation of alkanes (NCERT) gives different products depending on the reagent and conditions.
A: $\mathrm{CH_4 + O_2 \xrightarrow{Mo_2O_3,\Delta} HCHO + H_2O}$ gives an aldehyde, not an alcohol.
B: $\mathrm{2CH_3CH_3 + 3O_2 \xrightarrow{(CH_3COO)_2Mn,\Delta} 2CH_3COOH + 2H_2O}$ gives a carboxylic acid.
C: $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3CH \xrightarrow{KMnO_4} (CH_3)_3COH}$ oxidises the tertiary C–H bond, giving 2-methylpropan-2-ol, an alcohol.
D: $\mathrm{2CH_4 + O_2 \xrightarrow{Cu,\,523\,K,\,100\,atm} 2CH_3OH}$ gives methanol, an alcohol.
E: $\mathrm{CH_3CH{=}CHCH_3 \xrightarrow{KMnO_4/H^+} 2CH_3COOH}$ cleaves the double bond, giving an acid.
So the alcohol-forming reactions are C and D only.
Answer: (D) C and D Only

questions.stem: Amongst the following, the total number of compounds soluble in aqueous NaOH at room temperature is

image.alt: Figure for this Alcohols Phenols And Ethers question

questions.solution:
Concept: A compound dissolves in aqueous NaOH if it has an O–H acidic enough to be deprotonated by $OH^-$ (phenols, $pK_a\approx10$; carboxylic acids, $pK_a\approx4$–$5$). Alcohols ($pK_a\approx16$–$18$) are not deprotonated enough.
(I) Benzaldehyde has no acidic H, so it does not dissolve.
(II) 1-Naphthol is a phenol: $ArOH + NaOH \rightarrow ArO^-Na^+ + H_2O$. It dissolves.
(III) 4-(Dimethylamino)phenol is a phenol, so it dissolves.
(IV) p-Cresol is a phenol, so it dissolves.
(V) Benzoic acid forms sodium benzoate, so it dissolves.
(VI) N,N-Dimethylcyclohexylamine is a base with no acidic H, so it does not dissolve.
(VII) 1-Naphthoic acid is a carboxylic acid and forms its sodium salt, so it dissolves.
(VIII) 1,4-Di-tert-butylbenzene is a hydrocarbon, so it does not dissolve.
(IX) 1-Naphthylmethanol is an alcohol ($pK_a\approx16$), so it does not dissolve.
Count: II, III, IV, V and VII dissolve, giving a total of 5.
Answer: (A) 5

questions.stem:
Consider compounds A, B and C with following structural formula
$A=\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{OH}$
$B=\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$
$C=\mathrm{HO}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})-\mathrm{CH}_3$
For the conversion of B from A , reagent (D) required is _____ and structural formula of product (E) obtained when C undergoes same reaction using excess reagent (D) is _____
questions.solution:
A (pentan-1-ol, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2CH_2OH}$) → B (pent-1-ene, $\mathrm{CH_2{=}CHCH_2CH_2CH_3}$) is a loss of water: dehydration.
Alcohols are dehydrated by heating with a protic acid: conc. $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ (about $443\ \mathrm{K}$) or 85% $\mathrm{H_3PO_4}$. The $\mathrm{-OH}$ is protonated, water leaves and a β-H is removed to form $\mathrm{C{=}C}$.
PCC is an oxidising agent: it would give pentanal, not an alkene. So options B and C are ruled out.
C is butane-1,3-diol, $\mathrm{HO{-}CH_2CH_2CH(OH)CH_3}$. With excess acid, both $\mathrm{-OH}$ groups are removed by dehydration.
C-1 $\mathrm{-OH}$ is lost with H from C-2; C-3 $\mathrm{-OH}$ is lost with H from C-4.
$$\mathrm{HO{-}CH_2CH_2CH(OH)CH_3 \xrightarrow{\text{excess conc. } H_2SO_4,\ \Delta} CH_2{=}CH{-}CH{=}CH_2 + 2H_2O}$$
So E is buta-1,3-diene.
Option D is the only one giving the correct reagent (conc. $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ or $\mathrm{H_3PO_4}$). Its printed product appears garbled; the correct product is buta-1,3-diene.
Answer: (D) — D = conc. $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ or $\mathrm{H_3PO_4}$; E = $\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH{-}CH{=}CH_2}$

questions.stem:
One mole of phenol is treated with dilute $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ at 298 K to give a mixture of products. The mixture is separated by steam distillation. The seam volatile compound (X) is separated. The increase in percentage of oxygen in (X) with respect to phenol is ____ $10^{-1}$
(Given molar mass in $\mathrm{g} \; \mathrm{mol}^{-1} \; \mathrm{H}: 1, \; \mathrm{C}: 12, \; \mathrm{N}: 14$, O:16)
questions.solution:
Dilute $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ nitrates phenol to give a mixture of o‑nitrophenol and p‑nitrophenol.
o‑Nitrophenol has an intramolecular hydrogen bond, so it is steam volatile. p‑Nitrophenol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds, so it is not. Therefore X is o‑nitrophenol, $\mathrm{C_6H_5NO_3}$.
Phenol ($\mathrm{C_6H_6O}$): $M = 72+6+16 = 94\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$
$\%\,\mathrm{O} = \frac{16}{94}\times100 = 17.02\%$
o‑Nitrophenol ($\mathrm{C_6H_5NO_3}$): $M = 72+5+14+48 = 139\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$
$\%\,\mathrm{O} = \frac{48}{139}\times100 = 34.53\%$
Increase: $34.53\% - 17.02\% = 17.51\% \approx 175\times10^{-1}\ \%$
Answer: 175

Consider the following reactions. Total number of electrons in the π bonds and lone pair of electrons in the product (X) is:
$\left( \underset{\text{overset}}{\underset{\vert}{\mathrm{C}}} \mathrm{CHO} \overset{\vert}{\mathrm{CH_2OH}} \mathrm{HOH} \right)_4 \xrightarrow[\text{(iii) Benzoyl chloride Anhyd. AlCl}_3]{\substack{\text{(ii) } \mathrm{V_2O_5} / 10-20 \,\text{atm} / 773 \,\text{K} \\ \text{(i) } \mathrm{HI}, \Delta }} \;\underset{\text{Major product}}{(X)}$$\underset{overset}{\underset{\vert}{\mathrm{C}}}{\mathrm{CHO}}{\overset{\vert}{CH_2OH}}(HOH)_4 \xrightarrow[(iii)Benzoyl chloride Anhyd.AlCl_3]{\substack{ (ii) V_2O_5/10-20atm\;773K \\ (i)HI,\Delta}}\;\underset{Major product}{(X)}$
questions.solution:
Starting compound is glucose, $\mathrm{CHO(CHOH)_4CH_2OH}$.
(i) Prolonged heating with $\mathrm{HI}$ reduces glucose completely to n-hexane, $\mathrm{CH_3(CH_2)_4CH_3}$.
(ii) $\mathrm{V_2O_5}$ at $773\ \text{K}$ and $10$–$20\ \text{atm}$ aromatises n-hexane (cyclisation + dehydrogenation) to benzene, $\mathrm{C_6H_6}$.
(iii) Friedel–Crafts acylation of benzene with benzoyl chloride and anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ gives benzophenone, $\mathrm{C_6H_5COC_6H_5}$ = X.
π electrons: two rings have $2\times3 = 6$ π bonds, and $\mathrm{C=O}$ has $1$ π bond, so $7$ π bonds $= 14$ electrons.
Lone-pair electrons: the carbonyl O has $2$ lone pairs $= 4$ electrons.
Total $= 14 + 4 = 18$ electrons.
Answer: (D) 18

questions.stem:
Consider the following reaction.
$+ \mathrm{HI} \longrightarrow$ Product
Statement I: In the above reaction, product formed will be a mixture of benzyl alcohol and iodobenzene.
Statement II: In the above reaction, the $-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{CH}_2-$ bond is cleaved to give the product.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

image.alt: Figure for this Alcohols Phenols And Ethers question

options.label: A
options.content: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

options.label: B
options.content: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

options.label: C
options.content: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

options.label: D
options.content: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.solution:
The ether is benzyl phenyl ether, $\mathrm{C_6H_5{-}O{-}CH_2{-}C_6H_5}$.
Step 1: HI protonates the ether oxygen to give $\mathrm{C_6H_5{-}\overset{+}{O}H{-}CH_2C_6H_5}$.
Step 2: The $\mathrm{C_6H_5{-}O}$ bond has partial double-bond character because the O lone pair is in resonance with the ring, and the carbon is $sp^2$. So $\mathrm{I^-}$ cannot attack the aryl carbon, and this bond is not cleaved.
Step 3: The $\mathrm{O{-}CH_2}$ bond breaks instead. Losing phenol leaves a resonance-stabilised benzyl carbocation (the reaction may also go by $S_N2$ at the $\mathrm{CH_2}$ carbon).
Step 4: $\mathrm{I^-}$ attacks the benzylic carbon:
$$\mathrm{C_6H_5OCH_2C_6H_5 + HI \longrightarrow C_6H_5OH + C_6H_5CH_2I}$$
Step 5: The products are phenol and benzyl iodide, not benzyl alcohol and iodobenzene. So Statement I is false.
Step 6: The bond that breaks is the $\mathrm{{-}O{-}CH_2{-}}$ bond. So Statement II is true.
Answer: (D)
